failure: a candidate overfit to the visible suite passes the train-only gate and is selected night after night.
confidence: high — the gap is stated.

title: Evaluators without a `test_format` get no per-test evidence at all
evidence: the builder returns `None`, never fabricated evidence (`crates/dream-core/src/testfmt.rs:543`); such evaluators are "judged by the receipt alone, no statistics" (`crates/dream-gate/src/pertest.rs:187`).
failure: a regression confined to such an evaluator is invisible to both the fingerprint veto and every policy veto; the change is promoted on the receipt alone.
confidence: high — stated.

title: Below `min_cases` the evaluator is one case, and `Floor` is candidate-only
evidence: below `min_cases` the evaluator counts as one case, judged by `NoRegression` and `Floor` only (`crates/dream-gate/src/pertest.rs:282`); `Floor` checks only candidate scores against the floor (`crates/pairwise-gate/src/policy.rs:156`).
failure: in a small evaluator, a candidate that degrades every score but stays above the floor and triggers no new fingerprint adds no veto.
confidence: high for the behaviour; medium for the harm.

title: A fault share of exactly 0.5 is tolerated: the rule runs on half-missing evidence
evidence: only a share larger than the limit is inconclusive; exactly at the limit is tolerated (`crates/pairwise-gate/src/model.rs:226`).
failure: an evaluator judged with half its pairings faulted proceeds to the rule on the remainder, treating a half-evacuated evidence base as sufficient.
confidence: high — stated as deliberate.

title: A corrupt cross-night manifest fails open and silently disables stuck-harness detection
evidence: a corrupt or absent manifest loads as empty (`crates/dream-core/src/streak.rs:124`, `:261`); from an empty manifest every current harness fault is `New`, and the stuck notice requires "some persisting, none new" (`crates/dream-core/src/streak.rs:76`, `:136`).
failure: a partial write or corruption erases history; a genuinely stuck testbed is reclassified as all-new every night and never escalated.
confidence: high — both halves stated.

title: A flapping fault is `New` forever, so stuck detection cannot fire for intermittent harness faults
evidence: `Fixed` → `New` on return with the count reset (`crates/failure-fingerprint/src/lib.rs:782`); the stuck notice requires some persisting records (`crates/dream-core/src/streak.rs:76`).
failure: a harness fault that recurs every other night is `New` on each return, never persisting, and is never escalated as stuck.
confidence: high for the mechanism; medium that it is a defect rather than intent.

title: `count` is cumulative, not consecutive; consumers must re-derive strictness themselves
evidence: `count` is the previous count plus one; callers needing strictness must check `prev.step + 1 == step` (`crates/failure-fingerprint/src/lib.rs:539`).
failure: a consumer reading `count` as consecutive nights overestimates streaks across gaps and mis-escalates.
confidence: high — stated debt.

title: Cross-night records are long-lived, which is where a 64-bit collision would matter
evidence: SEL-02.4 Open — the gate use needs only two trees, while the cross-night use "keeps records for as long as the failure persists"; the identity is 64 bits (`crates/failure-fingerprint/src/lib.rs:263`).
failure: two distinct harness faults sharing a fingerprint merge into one long-lived record; escalation and stuck classification are wrong indefinitely.
confidence: medium — the exposure is flagged by the authors; the occurrence is inferred.

title: Suspected: crate-level `NoRegression` does not treat baseline-pass → candidate-fault as a regression
evidence: a fault pairing "is never a win or a loss" (`crates/pairwise-gate/src/model.rs:205`); `NoRegression` is described only as pass→fail (`crates/pairwise-gate/src/policy.rs:364`); the SEL-01.3 Tension says faults "are caught separately by the harness veto at step 1", implying the policy layer does not handle them; nothing in the material states that pass→fault rejects.
failure: a candidate-side fault on a previously passing test escapes the crate policy and rests entirely on the per-test "any fault" check — the same check whose equivalence the authors doubt (see R-1).
confidence: medium, inferred — it is an absence of statement, not a statement.

title: In the gate, the improvement policies can only reject; `Select` is inert, so the per-test layer appears to require the absence of vetoes rather than positive evidence
evidence: only `Reject` is acted on (`crates/dream-gate/src/pertest.rs:304`); per-test evidence "can only add vetoes" (`crates/dream-gate/src/pertest.rs:12`); `Margin`, `SignTest` and `WilsonLower` are in the gate's stack (`crates/dream-gate/src/pertest.rs:326`) but their `Select` outcome has no stated effect there.
failure: a candidate that improves nothing, triggers no new fingerprint and no pass→fail transition accumulates no veto and passes — whether any other layer requires positive evidence is not stated in the material.
confidence: medium, inferred — the per-test behaviour is stated; the promotion semantics are not.

title: Task identity is part of the fingerprint, so task renaming makes known failures unmatchable
evidence: the identity hashes task, stage and cause (`crates/failure-fingerprint/src/lib.rs:357`); the gate rebuilds the baseline manifest from the baseline run each night (SEL-02.3, SEL-02.4 Open).
failure: the suite reindexes task names between the baseline and candidate runs; the candidate's known failures no longer match the baseline's, are all classed `New`, and good changes are falsely rejected — a chronic fail-closed condition.
confidence: medium, inferred — the mechanism is stated; the occurrence is not.

title: Any single fault anywhere raises a harness veto for the whole night
evidence: "any fault, or a baseline test missing on candidate" → harness veto, BLOCKED-ENV (`crates/dream-gate/src/pertest.rs:214`, `:232`).
failure: nightly promotions stall on any infra flake; the stated consequence is only blocking, but chronic blocking is the classic pressure that produces unvetted manual overrides — the override, not the block, would be the incident.
confidence: low, inferred — the blocking is stated; the override behaviour is not.

title: Truncation at 200 characters merges any long causes sharing a prefix
evidence: whitespace is collapsed and the cause truncated to 200 characters before hashing (`crates/failure-fingerprint/src/lib.rs:190`).
failure: two long, distinct causes (long stack traces with a shared header) are identical after truncation, share a fingerprint, and the second is hidden as `Persisting` — the same silent bypass as R-2 by a different route.
confidence: medium, inferred — the rule is stated; the merging follows from it.

title: Within one step, observations with the same fingerprint are de-duplicated, first wins
evidence: same-fingerprint observations in one step are de-duplicated, first wins (`crates/failure-fingerprint/src/lib.rs:562`).
failure: several genuinely distinct failures that normalise identically in one run collapse into one record; the count under-reports and, in the gate's step 2, the second failure is invisible if the first matched the baseline.
confidence: medium, inferred.
